data.text:
From Rob Rances
———————-

The questions are just beginning.

The LA County Medical Examiner has spoken.
• Cause of death: Cocaine effects
• Manner: Accidental
• Case status: Still open

But this isn’t just a private tragedy. It’s a PUBLIC CONCERN.

Because Paolo Tantoco wasn’t just a private citizen. He was a known figure in elite circles—and part of First Lady Liza Marcos’ entourage during the Manila International Film Festival. Soem reports say he was found dead in the exact same hotel where the FL’s circle stayed. Hours after the event. In foreign soil.

So let’s ask what they won’t:
• Was this his first exposure to cocaine?
• Who was with him? 
• Who else had access that night?
• Was he exposed to something he didn’t consent to?
• Was this preventable? Or worse—enabled?
• If it was an accident… then accidental for whom?

This is now a U.S. jurisdiction case. Which means:
• The hotel’s CCTV might hold answers.
• Toxicology reports could reveal more than cocaine.
• Members of the Philippine entourage may soon face questioning.

So why is Malacañang silent?
No statement? No clarification? No accountability? 

Why are we treating this as an isolated tragedy when the man was moving in the official circles of power?

If this happened within a Presidential circle abroad—transparency is not optional. 

Because the people deserve to know.
Is this just about one man? Or the circles of power he moved in?

This isn’t just about drugs.
It’s about power. And what happens when no one dares to look too closely.

We ought to ask hard questions because silence protects no one—except those who already have too much protection.

#PRCFireAlert | A first-alarm fire engulfed a residential area at Road 2, Brgy. Matandang Balara, Quezon City, on July 12 at 4:09 p.m.

The blaze damaged ten houses, affecting 15 families or 38 individuals.

In response, the PRC dispatched an ambulance with five personnel led by Glendyl Japones from the PRC Quezon City Chapter.

Four patients were treated, including a female senior citizen who was transported to Quezon City Memorial Medical Center due to left hip pain.

Fire out was declared at 5:25 p.m.

During emergencies, call the PRC hotline at 143.
